requestedActions.title: Read titles and content of Notion pages that each customer explicitly shares with the app

guide.summary: Customers in other workspaces must connect, so the integration needs to be public rather than workspace-scoped. Notion documents OAuth 2.0 for this, where each user authorizes the app and selects pages through the page picker. The read-only request maps to the Read content capability, which covers retrieving pages, page markdown and block children. Client credentials, redirect configuration and the token exchange are setup requirements, and Marketplace review is not required to start authorization. Setup and execution remain untested.

findings.title: OAuth 2.0 user authorization with per-user page selection
findings.detail: Each customer authorizes the app separately; Notion shows the capabilities prompt, the user selects pages via the page picker, and the app exchanges the returned code for a user-tied access token.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers connect their own Notion accounts and share selected pages with the app

evidence.quote: Use an OAuth integration when your internal tool needs to act on behalf of each person who uses it. Each user authorizes the app separately and grants it access to
a user-scoped static token, and OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
3 The user selects which pages to grant the connection access to using the page picker.

steps.title: Create a public OAuth integration in the Notion Developer portal
steps.detail: Create a new public connection (any workspace installation scope) with redirect URIs and the Read content capability only. Installation scope cannot be changed after creation, so choose public for customers in other workspaces.
steps.doneWhen: Developer portal shows a public OAuth integration with Read content capability, a configured redirect URI, and a client ID and client secret on the Configuration tab.
